sections.label: 2022 economic growth and unemployment
sections.summary: The economy grew 3.6% in 2022 and the December resident unemployment rate was 2.8%, below pre-pandemic levels.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: All in all, amidst a very challenging external backdrop, our economy grew by 3.6% in 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The resident unemployment rate, at 2.8% in December last year, is below pre-pandemic levels.

sections.label: Global inflation level
sections.summary: By the end of last year, global inflation was around 9%.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: By the end of last year, global inflation was around 9%.

sections.label: Cost-of-living support packages
sections.summary: Three packages totalling more than $3.5 billion were rolled out to address cost-of-living concerns, especially for lower- and middle-income groups.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: While this has helped ease the pressure on headline inflation, it is still higher than what Singaporeans are used to.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, to address cost-of-living concerns, I rolled out three packages last year, totalling more than $3.5 billion, extending comprehensive support to Singaporeans, especially the lower- and middle-income groups.

sections.label: Lower draw on Past Reserves
sections.summary: A lower amount of up to $3.1 billion is expected to be drawn from Past Reserves, bringing the FY2020 to FY2022 total to $40 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Because the public health situation has since stabilised, we now expect to draw a lower amount of up to $3.1 billion from Past Reserves.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This brings the total expected draw on Past Reserves from FY2020 to FY2022 to $40 billion.

sections.label: Slower 2023 growth forecast
sections.summary: Singapore expects positive but slower economic growth of 0.5% to 2.5% this year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Overall, based on current indications of global conditions, we expect positive, but slower, economic growth in Singapore of 0.5% to 2.5% this year.

sections.label: Extensions to business support schemes
sections.summary: The Enterprise Financing Scheme enhancements and the Energy Efficiency Grant are each extended for one year until 31 March 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will help businesses weather the immediate challenges of tighter financial conditions and higher energy prices.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will extend the current enhancements to the Enterprise Financing Scheme for another year till 31 March 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I hope this will also encourage financial institutions to continue extending credit to viable enterprises.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will also extend the Energy Efficiency Grant for one year until 31 March 2024.

sections.label: GSTV Cash quantum increases
sections.summary: GSTV Cash payouts will rise for residents in homes with annual values of $13,000 and below, and above $13,000 up to $21,000, in 2023 and from 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For those residing in homes with annual values of $13,000 and below, I will increase the GSTV Cash quantum from $500 to $700 in 2023, and to a further $850 from 2024 onwards.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For those residing in homes with annual values of above $13,000 and up to $21,000, I will increase the GSTV Cash quantum from $250 to $350 in 2023, and then to $450 from 2024 onwards.

sections.label: AP Cash and CDC Vouchers
sections.summary: AP Cash will increase by $300 to $650 for eligible Singaporeans, bringing total payments to $700 to $2,250 over five years, and CDC Vouchers will rise by $100 in 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We have completed the review and will make the following enhancements in this Budget.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will increase the AP Cash by between $300 and $650 for eligible Singaporeans over the remaining years of the AP.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This will bring the total AP Cash payments received by adult Singaporeans to between $700 and $2,250 over five years.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will increase the Community Development Council (CDC) Vouchers by $100 in 2024.

sections.label: Cost-of-Living Special Payment
sections.summary: A one-off Cost-of-Living Special Payment of $200 to $400 will be provided for each eligible adult Singaporean under the AP.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will, therefore, introduce additional one-off support measures this year under the AP.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will provide a Cost-of-Living Special Payment of between $200 and $400 for each eligible adult Singaporean.

sections.label: Child top-ups and AP cost
sections.summary: Children aged six and below get a $400 CDA top-up and older children a $300 Edusave or PSEA top-up, raising the AP cost to $3 billion and the Package to $9.6 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For households with children, I will provide each child aged six and below a top-up of $400 to their Child Development Account (CDA), and each older child a top-up of $300 to their Edusave account or Post-Secondary Education Account (PSEA).

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: These enhancements to the AP – all the enhancements I mentioned just now, both the one-off and the earlier ones – will cost $3 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, the total amount of the Package will increase from $6.6 billion to $9.6 billion.

sections.label: US-China technology contest
sections.summary: The US seeks a technological lead over China, banning high-end chips and chipmaking to China, while China invests in its own "little giants" for self-reliance.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The US, in particular, is determined to establish a clear technological lead over China, especially in critical industries like semiconductors and green energy.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: It has banned the flow of high-end chips and chipmaking to China, and is engaging its allies around the world to do the same.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: China, in turn, is investing in its own "little giants" to achieve technological self-reliance.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We are seeing a huge contest for leadership in key technologies, which is likely to escalate with time.

sections.label: Less hospitable world for Singapore
sections.summary: Countries are focusing more on national gain and security, making the world less hospitable to small economies like Singapore that rely on an open, rules-based multilateral system.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Countries are thinking less about mutual benefit and interdependence, and more about national gain and security.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: It will be a world that is less hospitable to small economies like Singapore, which have long thrived on an open, rules-based multilateral system.

sections.label: Forward Singapore exercise completion
sections.summary: The Forward Singapore exercise is to be completed in the second half of this year, with complex issues requiring further exploration.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: These are important but complex issues which require further exploration.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We aim to complete the Forward Singapore exercise in the second half of this year.

sections.label: National Productivity Fund top-up
sections.summary: The National Productivity Fund will be topped up with $4 billion and its scope expanded to include investment promotion.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We currently have the National Productivity Fund (NPF), which supports a wide range of measures for productivity enhancement, and continuing education and training (CET).

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will top up the NPF with $4 billion and expand the scope of the Fund to include investment promotion as a supportable activity.

sections.label: Enterprise Innovation Scheme tax deductions
sections.summary: A new Enterprise Innovation Scheme will raise tax deductions to 400% of qualifying expenditure on five activities.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This is why the Government has consistently committed resources to research and development (R&D).

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We are investing $25 billion from 2021 to 2025 to catalyse research, innovation and enterprise.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But innovation is not without risk, which businesses may find more difficult to take, amidst slower growth and higher cost.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, to help our businesses press on with innovation, I will introduce a new Enterprise Innovation Scheme (EIS).

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Today, businesses can enjoy tax deductions of up to 250% of qualifying expenditure on some of these activities.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will raise the tax deductions to 400% of qualifying expenditure on each of these five activities.

sections.label: Cash payout option for businesses
sections.summary: Businesses may convert 20% of total qualifying expenditure per Year of Assessment into a cash payout of up to $20,000.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: To cover these firms, I will allow businesses the option to convert 20% of their total qualifying expenditure per Year of Assessment into a cash payout of up to $20,000.

sections.label: Committed $1 billion investment
sections.summary: To date $1 billion has been committed and invested in about 60 Singapore-based companies.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: To date, we have committed $1 billion to this effort and invested in about 60 Singapore-based companies.

sections.label: SME Co-Investment Fund addition
sections.summary: An additional $150 million will be set aside via the SME Co-Investment Fund to invest in promising SMEs and catalyse $300 million in private investments.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Given the positive outcomes, I will set aside an additional $150 million via the SME Co-Investment Fund.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will use this to invest in promising SMEs and we will also aim to catalyse an additional $300 million of private investments to support our SMEs.

sections.label: Singapore Global Enterprises funding boost
sections.summary: The Budget sets aside $1 billion to further boost the Singapore Global Enterprises initiative introduced last year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In last year's Budget, I introduced the Singapore Global Enterprises (SGE) initiative to provide such companies with more dedicated and customised support.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will now set aside $1 billion to provide a further boost to this initiative.

sections.label: Jobs-Skills Integrators pilot sectors
sections.summary: Jobs-Skills Integrators will be piloted in precision engineering, retail and wholesale trade, sectors with more mature workers and SMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Most importantly, they must ensure that training translates into better employment and earnings prospects.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will pilot the Jobs-Skills Integrators in the precision engineering, retail and wholesale trade sectors, where there are higher concentrations of mature workers and SMEs.

sections.label: Senior employment support extensions
sections.summary: The Senior Employment Credit and Part-time Re-employment Grant are extended till 2025 to support employers hiring senior workers.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We want to encourage and support employers who recognise the value that seniors like Mr Rahmat offer, invest in them and enable them to keep earning a good living.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will, therefore, extend the Senior Employment Credit till 2025, to continue providing wage offsets to employers that hire senior workers.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will also extend the Part-time Re-employment Grant till 2025, to encourage employers to offer part-time re-employment, other flexible work arrangements (FWAs) and structured career planning to senior workers.

sections.label: PWCS, disability and ex-offender credits
sections.summary: The PWCS Fund is topped up by $2.4 billion, the Enabling Employment Credit enhanced, and a new Uplifting Employment Credit introduced.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And last June, I raised the Government's co-funding share for the 2022 PWCS.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will maintain the increase for this year and top up the PWCS Fund by $2.4 billion for this purpose.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: To support employers to hire persons with disabilities, or PwDs, I will enhance the Enabling Employment Credit to cover a larger proportion of wages and a longer duration for PwDs who have not been working for at least six months.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: As a society, we should give them the opportunity to do so.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will also introduce a new Uplifting Employment Credit in the form of a time-limited wage offset to encourage firms to employ ex-offenders.

sections.label: BTO ballot for first-timer families
sections.summary: First-timer families with children and young married couples get an additional ballot for their BTO flat applications.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Given this wide range of first-timer applicants, and the current tightness in BTO supply, we should identify and provide more support to specific groups.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will, therefore, focus on first-timer families with children, as well as young married couples aged 40 years old and below, who are buying their first home.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will do more to help such families secure their BTO flats in a timely manner, including by giving them an additional ballot for their BTO flat applications.

sections.label: CPF Housing Grant increase for resale flats
sections.summary: The CPF Housing Grant rises by $30,000 for eligible first-timer families buying 4-room or smaller resale flats and $10,000 for larger flats.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will also provide more support for first-timer families to purchase resale flats.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will increase the Central Provident Fund (CPF) Housing Grant by $30,000 for eligible first-timer families purchasing 4-room or smaller resale flats and by $10,000 for those purchasing 5-room or larger flats.

sections.label: Housing grants for resale flats
sections.summary: Eligible families can receive up to $190,000 in grants when buying a resale flat, with the Enhanced CPF Housing Grant and Proximity Housing Grant.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Together with the Enhanced CPF Housing Grant and the Proximity Housing Grant, eligible families can receive up to $190,000 in grants when buying a resale flat.

sections.label: Baby Bonus Cash Gift increase
sections.summary: The Baby Bonus Cash Gift will increase by $3,000 for all eligible Singaporean children born from today onwards.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: While we make these adjustments, I will, at the same time, significantly increase financial support in the child's early years.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will increase the Baby Bonus Cash Gift by $3,000 for all eligible Singaporean children born from today onwards.

sections.label: Grant extension for new babies
sections.summary: The Grant will be extended to babies born from 1 October 2022 to 13 February 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This was for children born from 1 October 2020 to 30 September 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, to ensure we do not miss out on some new parents, I will extend the Grant to babies born from 1 October 2022 to 13 February 2023.

sections.label: Doubling Government-Paid Paternity Leave
sections.summary: Government-Paid Paternity Leave will double from two weeks to four weeks for eligible working fathers of Singaporean children born on or after 1 January 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Because many studies, internationally and in Singapore, have shown that children with more involved fathers have better physical, cognitive and emotional developmental outcomes.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will, therefore, double the Government-Paid Paternity Leave from two weeks to four weeks for eligible working fathers of Singaporean children born on or after 1 January 2024.

sections.label: Paternity and infant care leave
sections.summary: Unpaid Infant Care Leave will increase from six days to 12 days per year for each parent in the child's first two years.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: With the doubling of paternity leave, I hope the message is clear: we want paternal involvement to be the norm in our society and we will stand behind all our fathers who want to play a bigger role in raising our children.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will also increase Unpaid Infant Care Leave for each parent in the child's first two years, from the current six days per year to 12 days per year.

sections.label: Cost of family support enhancements
sections.summary: The enhancements to the Baby Bonus Cash Gift, CDA, and leave provisions will cost the Government an additional $240 million per birth cohort.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The enhancements to the Baby Bonus Cash Gift, CDA, and leave provisions will cost the Government an additional $240 million per birth cohort of children.

sections.label: Top up Fund for lower-income families
sections.summary: The Fund will be topped up by $300 million to support lower-income families in a high-inflation environment.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: To ensure that the Fund is able to provide the necessary support to our lower-income families in this high-inflation environment, I will top up the Fund by $300 million.

sections.label: Scaling up KidSTART nationwide
sections.summary: KidSTART will be scaled up nationwide to support 80% of eligible children in lower-income families, starting with children born this year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: To support more lower-income families with their children's early development, we will scale up KidSTART nationwide.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We expect to support 80% of eligible children in lower-income families, starting from the children born this year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Over the last decade, our spending on the early childhood sector has grown to six times its original size, from $320 million in FY2013 to about $1.9 billion in FY2022.

sections.label: Top ups for seniors' care funds
sections.summary: The ElderCare Fund will be topped up by $500 million and MediFund by $1.5 billion to support seniors' care and medical bills.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In the meantime, we will increase the resources dedicated to supporting seniors, especially lower-income seniors, with their long-term care and healthcare needs.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will top up the ElderCare Fund by $500 million to support means-tested subsidies for seniors who need home-based, centre-based or institutional care.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will also top up the MediFund by $1.5 billion to strengthen the safety net for lower-income individuals and seniors facing financial difficulties with their medical bills, even after Government subsidies, MediShield Life and MediSave.

sections.label: CPF contributions for younger Platform Workers
sections.summary: Platform Workers below 30 years old when the changes are implemented will be required to make increased CPF contributions.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Platform Workers who are below 30 years old when the changes are implemented will be required to make increased CPF contributions.

sections.label: CPF Transition Support for Platform Workers
sections.summary: For the first four years after implementation, lower-income Platform Workers facing higher CPF contribution rates will receive CPF Transition Support.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For the first four years after implementation, I will provide a CPF Transition Support to lower-income Platform Workers who see an increase in their CPF contribution rates.

sections.label: Minimum CPF payout for Retirement Sum Scheme
sections.summary: The minimum CPF monthly payout for seniors on the Retirement Sum Scheme will be increased to $350 a month.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In addition, I will increase the minimum CPF monthly payout for seniors on the Retirement Sum Scheme to $350 a month.

sections.label: Monthly salary ceiling raise
sections.summary: The monthly salary ceiling will be raised from $6,000 to $8,000 in 2026 to keep pace with rising salaries.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: To keep pace with rising salaries, we will raise the monthly salary ceiling from $6,000 to $8,000 in 2026.

sections.label: ACE Group for migrant workers
sections.summary: The Assurance, Care and Engagement Group was set up under MOM to monitor migrant worker dormitories and provide better care and support.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Learning from this, we have set up the Assurance, Care and Engagement Group, or the ACE Group, under the Ministry of Manpower (MOM), and we have built up its capabilities to monitor the situation in our migrant worker dormitories and provide better care and support for our migrant workers.

sections.label: Food and energy supply resilience
sections.summary: Singapore diversified import sources, stockpiled food and essential items, and built local production, enabling it to weather recent disruptions.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For some time now, we have been diversifying import sources, stockpiling food and essential items, and where possible, building up local production, like our "30 by 30" plan – to produce 30% of our nutritional needs locally by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: These efforts have enabled us to weather through the disruptions of the last three years.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We quickly stood up a Standby LNG Facility when the world scrambled for gas after the Russian invasion of Ukraine.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We had ample stock of frozen chicken when Malaysia banned the export of live chickens.

sections.label: Adapting to rising sea levels
sections.summary: A polder is being built at Pulau Tekong, and a Coastal and Flood Protection Fund was set up with $5 billion to support coastal and drainage infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And that means taking steps to adapt to global warming and especially to rising sea levels.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We are now building a polder at Pulau Tekong – it is already more than halfway complete and is set to finish by end-2024.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The experience gained from this project will give us more options to protect our coastline against rising sea levels.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We have also set up a Coastal and Flood Protection Fund with an initial injection of $5 billion to support the construction of coastal and drainage infrastructure.

sections.label: Giving.sg donations during pandemic
sections.summary: Donations through Giving.sg were about three times higher than pre-pandemic levels and remained around $100 million in the last three years.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Despite the economic downturn due to COVID-19, the donations received through Giving.sg were about three times higher than pre-pandemic levels and have remained at around $100 million in the last three years.

sections.label: Tax deduction and corporate volunteering
sections.summary: The tax deduction rate is extended three years till end-2026, and the Business and IPC Partnership Scheme will become a broader Corporate Volunteer Scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, we will extend this tax deduction rate for another three years till end-2026 and we will review thereafter what would be a more sustainable level of tax deduction for the longer term.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Many are already doing so, going beyond cash donations to skills-based volunteering and inclusive hiring.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will enhance the existing Business and IPC Partnership Scheme into a broader Corporate Volunteer Scheme, which will be rolled out for three years.

sections.label: Community Silver Trust top-up
sections.summary: The Budget tops up the Community Silver Trust by $1 billion, with $10 million more for Self-Help Groups over three years.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In this Budget, I will top up the Community Silver Trust by $1 billion to support our SSAs that deliver community care services for our seniors.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Charities and SSAs can also continue to tap on the Charities Capability Fund and the Community Capability Trust to drive innovation and transform their operations.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will also provide a $10 million top-up to the Self-Help Groups over the next three years.

sections.label: Higher property buyer stamp duties
sections.summary: Higher BSD rates apply to residential and non-residential property portions above set values for properties acquired from tomorrow, raising $500 million yearly.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For residential properties, the portion of the value of the property in excess of $1.5 million and up to $3 million would be taxed at 5%; while that in excess of $3 million would be taxed at 6%, up from the current rate of 4%.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The changes are expected to affect 15% of residential properties.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For non-residential properties, the portion of the value of the property in excess of $1 million and up to $1.5 million would be taxed at 4%; while that in excess of $1.5 million would be taxed at 5%, up from the current rate of 3%.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The changes to the BSD regime will apply to all properties acquired from tomorrow.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This is expected to generate an additional $500 million in revenue per year.

sections.label: Higher ARF for expensive cars
sections.summary: Cars with OMV above $40,000 pay higher marginal ARF rates, with the highest tier rising to 320% from 220%.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Buyers of cars with Open Market Value (OMV) of more than $40,000 will pay higher marginal ARF rates than they do today and, in particular, for the highest OMV tier, the revised ARF rates will be 320%, up from 220% today.

sections.label: BEPS Pillar Two minimum tax rate
sections.summary: Pillar Two of BEPS introduces a global minimum effective tax rate of 15% for large MNE groups.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Pillar Two of BEPS will introduce a global minimum effective tax rate of 15% for large MNE groups.

sections.label: Pillar Two implementation in 2025
sections.summary: Pillar Two will be implemented from 2025 with a Domestic Top-up Tax topping up MNE groups' Singapore effective tax rate to 15%.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Given these developments, I intend to implement Pillar Two from 2025, as part of the broader international move to align minimum global corporate tax rates for large MNE groups.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: When we do so, we will implement a Domestic Top-up Tax, which will top up the MNE groups' effective tax rate in Singapore to 15%.

sentences.text: For FY2023, I expect an overall slight deficit of $0.4 billion, or 0.1% of GDP.

sections.summary: The balance of the Contingencies Funds will be reduced from $16 billion to $6 billion with the return to normalcy.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: With the return to normalcy, I will reduce the balance of the Contingencies Funds from $16 billion to $6 billion.

sections.label: Volunteers helping vulnerable families
sections.summary: A volunteer and fellow volunteers delivered grocery packs and shared kueh bangkit with vulnerable families, showing mutual responsibility.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: During the pandemic, she and her fellow volunteers helped to deliver grocery packs to the elderly and lower-income families in her community.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: She also used her CDC vouchers, not for herself, but to buy "kueh bangkit" from her neighbourhood bakery and shared them with vulnerable families over the Lunar New Year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We have seen it in action and experienced it in abundance over the last three years – how we are responsible for one another, keep an eye out for our fellow citizens, and always band together as a team.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And as one united people, we can move forward with confidence in this new era, and shape a brighter future and a better Singapore together.
